39031.rationale: Reviewed all ten IDs against both other seed versions, including every supplied title, complete description, keyword, distribution title/description/format, publisher and optional spatial field; no temporal fields were supplied. Measurement concepts and units are preserved per ID: a001/a002 insect count, treatment and rate; a003 count/treatment only; a004 count only; a005 operational month/site/count only; a006/a007 mass/area/season; a008 mass/area only; a009 mass only; a010 mass/area/season in PDF only. Unlisted treatment rates, seasons and areas are not inferred. All CSV descriptions identify comma-separated tables, JSON descriptions identify JSON records with the same columns, and both PDF distributions of a010 identify PDF tables; no metadata format/content conflict was found. Verification is of supplied metadata association, not fetched file bytes. The forbidden positive tokens arthropod/suppression and orchard/productivity are absent from the corresponding supplied records. No frozen no-answer conjunction or explicit answer-key/intent/grade leakage appears. All identity_review_required flags are false; identity values are null because no authoritative identity audit is assigned here. Same-intent pairs a001/a002 and a006/a007 have distinct titles, locations and numeric examples rather than identical complete records. Wording varies beyond title substitution: a001's description directly lists measurements here, whereas 39032/39033 place them only in distributions; a002 and a004 are much longer here, while a003 and a006 expand in other seeds. Nevertheless strict factual preservation is not established: a001 distributions.0.description says insects counted per inspected tree (count; e.g. 14) and treatment application volume (litres/hectare; e.g. 3.28), versus count 10/rate 10.03 in 39032 and count 26/rate 6.48 in 39033. Its description location changes from Silver Creek Central to Oak Terrace Upper to Quartz Field Lower. Numeric examples change in every ID across seeds, and publisher/location context changes too. These are substantive text facts, not mere paraphrases, even though measurement concepts remain stable. a005's unresolved crop-tree versus warehouse-bag material ambiguity also persists across all three versions. No query text is supplied, so actual paraphrase equivalence and exact-lookup query semantics cannot be independently assessed from intent identifiers alone; corpus-wide coverage outside these ten IDs is not claimed. Formulaic catalogue-style titles recur; none supplies an authoritative SKU, hidden label or different measured fact. If strict policy treats these recurrent prose shells as template-only titles, that style boundary needs adjudication rather than an inferred acceptance.

Distribution titles are generic, but each description supplies the appropriate same-record columns and serialization. Metadata format/content association is verified, not actual file bytes. All records have meaningful changes in description ordering, verbosity, paragraph structure, title wording and optional spatial presence; examples include a003 moving its count/treatment list into a longer description here, a006 expanding with units and reuse notes, and a007 becoming a short distribution-directed synopsis. However changing reported examples and study context prevents an unconditional facts-preserved finding: a006 distributions.0.description documents harvested bean mass (kg; e.g. 565.11) and harvested plot area (hectares; e.g. 2.7), versus mass 873.5/area 7.02 in 39031 and mass 181/area 3.27 in 39033. a005 completed operations changes from 60 to 22 to 89, with facility location codes Hazel Ridge Inner, Dune Valley Central and Fern Hollow Outer. a002 pest count stays 21, but its application-rate examples change from 10.81 to 7.28 to 7.53 litres/hectare. The examples are marked e.g.; this limits their interpretation as actual rows, but does not make their literal numeric content preserved. a005 also continues to leave warehouse-bag contents unspecified while saying cacao trees grown as a crop. That ambiguity is not resolved by lexical similarity. Repeated catalogue-title prose shells are observable, not a factual variation guarantee; a strict template-only-title interpretation remains a style-policy uncertainty.
